_comment: Deterministic stub output for the NDA case. Coverage is near perfect while severity judgment is not, which is the failure mode aggregate scores hide. It catches the perpetual term, the over-broad definition and the residuals clause, but under-rates the consent-before-compelled-disclosure defect and the free assignment to a competitor, misses the notices point entirely, invents an indemnification clause the agreement does not contain, and fabricates the citation supporting a deemed-delivery rule.

clauses.text: Defines Confidential Information broadly, including unmarked information.
Receiving Party must keep information secret and not disclose without consent.
Return or destroy on request within 30 days.
Governed by the laws of Germany.
Legally compelled disclosure is permitted subject to prior written consent.
Unaided memory residuals may be used, including for third parties.
No licence granted in the disclosing party's intellectual property.
Injunctive relief available in addition to damages.
Receiving Party may assign to any third party without consent.
Notices effective when sent by email.
Receiving Party indemnifies the Disclosing Party for any breach.

risk_flags.rationale: A perpetual confidentiality term with no survival period is unenforceable in substance.
Unaided-memory residuals usable for third parties defeat the confidentiality obligation.
Definition covers unmarked information and lacks standard carve-outs.
Requiring consent before a compelled disclosure is unusual drafting.
Broad assignment rights are common in commercial agreements.

citations.quote: whether or not marked as confidential
shall keep all Confidential Information secret
shall remain in effect in perpetuity
return or destroy all Confidential Information in its possession within thirty (30) days
the laws of the Federal Republic of Germany
first obtains the prior written consent of the Disclosing Party

including a competitor of the disclosing counterparty
